post.photo: Three pairs of the children's shoes by the front door, lined up smallest to biggest. No people, no faces, no child. 1080 x 1350. Take it Sunday evening or Monday before 09:30.
post.instagram:
Three pairs of shoes by the front door, in three sizes.

Our eldest is eleven. Our youngest is four. And the fair question, the one any sensible person would ask, is why we do not just keep all of it away from them until they are sixteen.

We understand the pull of that. For years, keeping it away was our answer too.

But the longer we looked at it, the more a sixteenth birthday looked like a cliff edge. Nothing, nothing, nothing, then everything at once, with no practice.

So that is not what we do in our house. Not everything kept away. Not a free for all either. The bit in between: a little more freedom at each stage, earned, with us close by while the judgement grows.

It is slower. It is the only version we could picture working for all three of them.

What is one thing you were handed all at once that you wish you had been given a bit at a time?
